prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application concept for Wicker Study Tutor, 1440 × 900 landscape
Primary request: Design the "Tutor Workbench" page as a credible production UI, not a poster. This is a workspace-wide academic tutor that explains course material, answers questions about syllabi and announcements, checks schedule and progress, creates practice sets, and proposes planning changes only after consent.
Input image: existing Wicker Study Practice page; carry over its exact app shell, warm off-white canvas, left sidebar, Archivo/Archivo Narrow feeling, navy ink, indigo action color, thin full-span rules, corner language and density. Do not copy Practice content.
Composition: keep the existing Wicker left navigation. Main Tutor area is one broad centered document-like conversation sheet, with no permanent right rail. Header: large "Tutor", compact scope control "Workspace-wide", a subdued context note "All courses and connected sources", and buttons "New conversation" and "History". Under it, a horizontal opener strip with three plain ruled prompts: "Explain a topic", "Check a requirement", "Plan around a conflict".
Show a conversation about "Why does Dijkstra’s algorithm fail with negative edges?" The assistant response is generous and pedagogical: short direct answer, a small clean graph diagram area, a numbered explanation, and an inline action link "Create a 10-question practice set". Under the answer, show three full-width disclosure rows whose borders span the sheet edge to edge: "Sources · 4", "What I used from your course · BCS1540", and "Suggested action · Create practice set". The Sources row is collapsed. The Suggested action row is expanded into a quiet consent review band stating course, topics, question mix, and estimated duration, with secondary "Cancel" and primary indigo "Create practice set". Do not use nested cards.
Bottom: fixed full-width composer within the main content, with a visible context line "Workspace-wide" and a removable route-aware chip "Looking at BCS1540 · Greedy Algorithms". Include attachment and send controls.
Visual hierarchy: explanatory answer first, interactive teaching artifact second, disclosures third. User messages can be compact; assistant messages are not bubbles. Use full-span internal dividers that always reach containing edges. Avoid borders ending within padding, gradients, glass, excessive shadows, bento cards, oversized blank areas, or playful illustration. Keep text legible and exact. The page must unmistakably feel like a serious academic workbench.
